purpose: Screen memory mechanisms for long-running agent tasks.
claims: Private, constructed development tests. No breakthrough or general performance claim.

model_calls.note: The preflight used 13080 input tokens for a short prompt. Packet size is separate from total native usage.

experiments.hypothesis: A typed ledger preserves critical information better than recursive prose at the same token target.
A rule-and-exception packet predicts unseen cases better than an ordinary summary, while retaining uncertainty in unsupported cases.
A small pretrained model updated on verified answers provides useful queryable memory after a small training budget.
Query-conditioned retrieval preserves more answer-relevant facts than one global compact packet at a matched reader-context target.
A checkpoint with pending actions and verification state supports correct task resumption better than a knowledge-only summary.
A source-backed preservation check followed by repair reduces errors on independent questions after aggressive compaction.
E4's retrieval answers remain correct when each query and context are isolated from all other queries.
experiments.phase: adaptive diagnostic on the known E4 fixture

experiments.hypothesis: E2's prediction questions require the transferred memory rather than the questions and prior knowledge alone.
experiments.phase: adaptive control on the known E2 fixture

shared_limits: Researchers construct both tasks and graders; this is not an independent benchmark.
Tests do not reproduce an entire native IDE agent workflow.
Small samples screen mechanisms; they do not establish statistical superiority.
All calls, failures, setup costs, and unavailable usage remain in records.
A random tiny model is not evidence for a capable pretrained tiny LLM.
Training and reader inference costs must be reported separately from packet tokens.
